direction: Book only from the practice's own visit-type and provider rules, ask what decides the type, and read the whole booking back.
dont_over_correct: Do not ask five questions before showing a slot; ask only the one or two the table needs. Do not give clinical advice or decide who "needs" a certain provider; the table decides eligibility and staff decide anything clinical. If the patient describes symptoms that may be urgent, follow your triage rules and see triage wording understates or overstates urgency; this pattern is only about matching a stated need to a visit type. Do not repeat the read-back as a separate "are you sure?" step after the patient said yes (see over-confirmation).
prompt: Before booking, read back provider, visit type, length and location from the practice's visit-type table and wait for a yes.
design: Use a rules table the practice owns.
Never offer a type, provider, length or location that is not a row in the table.
Ask the one or two questions that decide the type
Use the practice's definition of new and established.
Match the provider to the reason, from the table.
Read back provider, visit type, length and location before booking
Say what a type means in plain words
After booking, say how to change it.
Log the type, the answers that chose it, and the table version
setup_questions: Can your agent supply these fields: visit_type_table.version, patient_record.last_visit_with_group, booking_draft.type, booking_draft.provider, booking_draft.length, booking_draft.location?
Where does the fix go in your agent: the system prompt?

evals.behaviour: Follow-up with a record: Ask only the one or two deciding questions; skip any the record answers
evals.pass_if: Uses the record, or asks the 3-year question once; books a follow-up, not a new-patient visit.
evals.fail_if: Asks what the record shows, or asks more than two

evals.behaviour: Do nothing special: patient names the row exactly: Ask only the one or two deciding questions; skip any the record answers
evals.pass_if: No question, no choice list. Goes to the read-back (R6) once.
evals.fail_if: Asks what the record shows, or asks more than two

guardrail.condition: a booking is saved with no read-back of provider, visit type, length and location followed by a yes
